nodes.plm_action: Wiping off dirt and grime from engine components using a cloth
nodes.plm_caption: The video shows an engine compartment of a machine. The engine compartment is being shown from several different angles. A yellow tag is held up by a hand in the background. It reads "OUT OF SERVICE" and there is other writing on the sign too.

summary.brief: A man in an orange jumpsuit disassembles a Hyster forklift engine, exposing a slack belt and four bent exhaust valves.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the presenter standing beside an opened forklift engine compartment, holding a wrench. He removes the rocker cover to reveal large exhaust valves and notes that the drive belt, although still on the pulleys, is loose and flappy because it has jumped teeth and smashed several exhaust‑side valves. He then clears clutter by pulling aside hoses and the intake manifold, loosens and removes the head bolts, and lifts the cylinder head off the block. The head shows no warpage and the gasket remains intact, but four exhaust valves are visibly bent. Throughout the segment a yellow “OUT OF SERVICE” tag is held up in the background, and the engine is shown from several angles as the work progresses.

action.detailed: Take off the rocker cover, detach the intake manifold, loosen and remove the head bolts, then lift the cylinder head off the block to examine the slack belt and the bent exhaust valves.
action.actor: the man wearing an orange jumpsuit

nodes.plm_action: Remove air filter

In the back of the vehicle is a man in orange standing next to the forklift and looking around.  The lighting is good. In the background there is a white truck.

summary.brief: Man in an orange jumpsuit examines the open engine of a yellow forklift.
summary.detailed: The handheld video shows a yellow forklift parked outdoors beside a white truck with its engine cover already removed. A man wearing an orange jumpsuit stands in front of the open machine, places his right hand on the left side of the air‑filter, steps back, walks away, then returns and moves closer to the forklift while looking into the exposed compartment. The camera captures the interior components – wires, hoses, a battery and a large grey tube that runs across the middle and turns upward to the right – as the man inspects them.

action.detailed: Inspect the forklift's open engine by placing a hand on the air filter, stepping back, then moving closer to view the wires, hoses, battery and large grey tube inside the compartment.
action.actor: a man wearing an orange jumpsuit

nodes.plm_action: removing the old valve
nodes.plm_caption: The video is focused on the inside of an engine. You can see the battery, various wires and a bunch of engine parts. The pistons on the cylinder head have gaskets that can be seen separately.

summary.brief: The presenter removes the rocker cover and cylinder head of the forklift engine, exposing bent exhaust valves, a slack drive belt and the bare engine block before showing the disassembled components.
summary.detailed: Starting with the rocker cover removed, the presenter points out the oversized exhaust valves and a drive belt that is still on but loose and mis‑aligned. He explains that the belt has jumped after many hours, causing the valves to clash and become bent. He then loosens the head bolts, lifts the cylinder head off, and shows four bent exhaust‑side valves while the rest of the head looks undamaged and the gasket is intact. After clearing the intake manifold and other hardware, the surrounding parts are dumped onto the floor. The camera pans over the pile of bolts, covers, and hoses, then focuses on the exposed engine block lying on a grey surface, noting its dirt, rust, and drained oil. Throughout, the presenter comments on the lack of belt tension, the absence of major warpage, and how the forklift lacks a drive coupling, ending with a brief overview of the fully disassembled engine and a promise of future updates.

action.detailed: Unscrew the head bolts, lift off the rocker cover and cylinder head, inspect the damaged exhaust valves, clear away the scattered parts, and display the exposed engine block.
action.actor: a man wearing an orange jumpsuit

summary.detailed: The handheld camera follows the man as he lifts off the forklift’s rocker cover, exposing oversized exhaust‑valve faces that are smashed and a drive belt that is still on the pulleys but flappy and mis‑aligned. He points out the lack of belt tension and the damaged valves, then proceeds to loosen and remove the bolts holding the intake manifold and the cylinder head. After the bolts are cleared, he pulls the head back enough to view the interior, revealing four bent exhaust‑side valves while the surrounding wiring, hoses and filters remain visible.

A yellow “OUT OF SERVICE” tag is visible in the background. Natural daylight provides dull but sufficient illumination as the presenter gestures to each component and comments on their condition.

summary.detailed: The handheld camera pans across the open forklift engine bay, showing the battery, wiring, hoses and the exposed engine block. A man steps into view, points at components and inserts his hand into the compartment. He grasps the bolts that hold the rocker/cylinder‑head cover, turning each counter‑clockwise to loosen and remove the cover. With the cover off, the camera shows several smashed exhaust‑side valves and a drive belt that has lost tension and hangs loosely. He continues to turn a few more bolts while the camera sweeps over the jumble of wires and metal parts, then pulls back to give a wider view of the entire engine before the segment ends with a brief close‑up of the engine as smoke drifts from it.

He picks up a loose part from the floor and examines it, then points to a belt on the engine while a close‑up shows a large pulley moving back and forth. The camera pans across the engine bay, revealing a blue transparent bowl filled with parts, a white container of dark material, and a cloth tucked in the corner. Next, the mechanic touches a small metal component with his right hand while holding an electrical wire with his left. Finally, a close‑up of the underside of the engine beneath the radiator shows rusty parts, the mechanic’s hand gripping a ratchet near gears, and water spraying from the area.

Gudday Everybody. This hyster doesnt run, me and dan picked it up cheap. damn wasteful companies. anyway, see how we go...

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video begins with the presenter standing beside an opened forklift engine compartment, holding a wrench. He removes the rocker cover to reveal large exhaust valves and notes that the drive belt, although still on the pulleys, is loose and flappy because it has jumped teeth and smashed several exhaust‑side valves. He then clears clutter by pulling aside hoses and the intake manifold, loosens and removes the head bolts, and lifts the cylinder head off the block. The head shows no warpage and the gasket remains intact, but four exhaust valves are visibly bent. Throughout the segment a yellow “OUT OF SERVICE” tag is held up in the background, and the engine is shown from several angles as the work progresses.

Inspect head gasket and tighten engine bolts
Hold engine block and point to second motor

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
